question: What defines microbial surveillance in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Continuous tracking and analysis of disease data
options.B: Isolating infected patients in private wards
options.C: Treating individual patients with broad antibiotics
options.D: A one-time survey of hospital room cleanliness

explanation: Surveillance requires ongoing, systematic collection rather than isolated checks so trends can be monitored over time. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h1)

question: The primary link between individual patient care and public health authorities is provided by what process?
explanation: Individual diagnostic findings feed directly into broader surveillance systems to inform community health actions. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h1)

question: An early detection system in public health surveillance primarily helps with what task?

options.A: Reducing the cost of manufacturing new vaccines
options.B: Spotting unusual disease clusters before widespread transmission
options.C: Calculating monthly hospital staff salary budgets
options.D: Determining the exact cause of chronic heart failure

explanation: Catching disease clusters early allows health workers to contain outbreaks before they overwhelm local facilities. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h2)

question: Why is establishing a baseline level of pathogens important for a healthcare system?

options.A: It sets the standard price for laboratory diagnostic kits
options.B: It proves that the hospital is free of all bacteria
options.C: It helps identify unusual spikes that signal an outbreak
options.D: It dictates the required nursing shift schedule

explanation: Knowing the normal expected frequency of an illness makes abnormal increases immediately obvious. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which surveillance type relies on health workers submitting reports voluntarily or by routine mandate?
explanation: Passive systems wait for reports to come in from clinical sites, which keeps costs low but can miss mild or unrecorded cases. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h3)

question: Public health staff actively searching clinic records for disease cases describes which surveillance method?
explanation: Active surveillance requires staff to proactively hunt for data rather than waiting for reports to arrive. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using standardized case definitions in data collection?

options.A: Eliminating the need for patient consent forms
options.B: Reducing the cost of purchasing laboratory reagents
options.C: Speeding up the discharge process for surgical patients
options.D: Ensuring a disease is counted consistently across regions

explanation: Standard definitions ensure everyone uses the exact same criteria to classify a case, making data comparable. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h4)

question: A nurse forgets to chart a patient's positive malaria test result in the ward register. What is the direct effect of this omission on surveillance?

options.A: It changes the standardized case definition for the district
options.B: It automatically triggers an emergency facility lockdown
options.C: It distorts public health statistics by underreporting disease frequency
options.D: It increases the hospital funding allocation for malaria drugs

explanation: Incomplete charting means public health bodies miss crucial data, leading to inaccurate disease tracking. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h4)

question: Why are bedside nurses considered the frontline of disease surveillance?

options.A: They write the official national epidemiological textbooks
options.B: They directly observe initial symptoms and track patient changes daily
options.C: They are responsible for funding community health programs
options.D: They hold the authority to declare national health emergencies

explanation: Nurses spend the most time with patients, placing them in the best position to spot unusual health changes early. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h5)

question: What action should a nurse take upon noticing a sudden cluster of unusual symptoms in a ward?

options.A: Discharge all affected patients immediately without follow-up
options.B: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics without a doctor's order
options.C: Report the observation through proper epidemiological channels
options.D: Ignore the pattern until the hospital director mentions it

explanation: Prompt reporting allows facility management and public health teams to investigate potential outbreaks swiftly. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is the very first step taken when an outbreak is suspected?

options.B: Close down all public markets in the region
options.C: Verify the diagnosis and confirm the outbreak
options.D: Draft a new national healthcare policy

explanation: Health teams must first confirm the lab results and diagnosis before launching a full-scale investigation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h6)

question: Analyzing outbreak data by time, place, and person helps public health workers achieve what goal?

options.A: Determine the salary grades for investigative staff
options.B: Calculate the exact profit margins of the hospital
options.C: Find epidemiological links to identify the source
options.D: Design new architectural layouts for clinics

explanation: Looking at who is sick, where they live, and when symptoms started points investigators toward the source of infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h6)

question: Which factor commonly delays outbreak responses in resource-limited health systems?

options.A: Reliance on slow paper-based record systems
options.B: Too many advanced computerized diagnostic labs
options.C: An excess of highly trained epidemiological staff

explanation: Manual paperwork takes longer to transport and compile, delaying the detection of and response to disease spikes. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is a major consequence of lacking reliable laboratory infrastructure during surveillance?

options.A: Delayed or missed confirmation of infectious pathogens
options.B: Automatic computerization of all hospital records
options.C: Faster distribution of public health bulletins
options.D: Immediate elimination of all community disease vectors

explanation: Without functioning labs, health workers struggle to identify what germ is causing a spike in illnesses. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h7)
